analysis.title: US stocks enter correction territory
key_insights: The S&P 500 closed 20 November in correction territory, down 11.6% from its 6 October all-time high after a 3.7% drop on Friday.
Main driver is negative AI-trade sentiment. AI capex is hitting physical and financing constraints that UBS says will limit positive earnings revisions for tech AI beneficiaries.
NVIDIA co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang has departed and an SEC investigation into the company's accounting practices has been revealed, shaking investor confidence across the industry.
Other drivers are doubts over whether AI revenues justify the investment scale, and a more hawkish Fed. CIO expects two more Fed rate hikes through 1Q27.

UBS cannot rule out further downside but does not expect a bear market (decline above 20%). That would need materially higher recession risk or signs of an imminent AI capex pullback, neither of which looks likely now.

Historically, bull-market drawdowns above 10% were good buying opportunities. S&P 500 rose an average of 8%, 13%, 19% and 28% over the next 3, 6, 12 and 24 months. The very elevated VIX also suggests favorable risk/reward.
CIO recently downgraded US equities from Attractive to Neutral. It expects more moderate upside as earnings, GDP and AI capex growth shift from accelerating to decelerating.
As growth slows, returns typically shift from higher-risk to higher-quality stocks. For 2027 UBS advises using strength to reduce excess concentration and focusing on higher-quality areas.
Defensive and non-AI segments have fared better in the downdraft.

market_movers.rationale: CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang departed and an SEC investigation into accounting practices was revealed, which shook confidence across the AI industry.

sector_views.rationale: Downgraded from Attractive to Neutral. Growth drivers are decelerating but the environment remains supportive. Drawdown seen as a buying opportunity for patient investors.
AI capex faces physical and financing constraints limiting positive earnings revisions. Defensive and non-AI segments have outperformed.
As growth rates slow, returns typically shift from higher-risk to higher-quality stocks.

earnings_insights: UBS says AI capex constraints will limit positive earnings revisions for tech AI beneficiaries. Earnings growth is expected to shift from accelerating to decelerating.

macro_indicators.interpretation: CIO's expectation of a tighter policy path matches the more hawkish Fed tone and is a headwind for equity valuations.
The index is in correction territory, and a bear market would need a further drop beyond 20%.

risk_factors: Further downside cannot be ruled out because market bottoms are hard to pinpoint.
Materially higher recession risk could push the drawdown past 20%.
Signs of an imminent pullback in AI capital spending could push the drawdown past 20%.
A more hawkish Fed with a tighter policy path.
AI revenues may not justify the scale of investment.
The SEC investigation into NVIDIA's accounting and the CEO departure.
vol_and_positioning: The VIX is described as very elevated, which UBS says suggests favorable risk/reward for stocks.
UBS recommends using market strength to reduce excess concentration in portfolios.
